prd_visual_references.summary: Focusboard recovery and responsive reference board

gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `tauri_source_manifest` is unverified.

acceptance_requirements: PRD section 3 steps 1 through 7 and step 11 complete against the running desktop app with durable data, using a local mail sink in place of a production provider.
PRD sections 4.1 and 4.2 hold for the implemented account states: anonymous, registered-but-unverified, verified signed in, and signed out or expired.
PRD section 6.1 inbox rules hold for quick-add, keyboard capture, empty-title rejection, and no-reload appearance, and section 6.2 holds for project create, rename, and the list view.
Entities implemented this slice have one authoritative server representation, and a rejected mutation reconciles visibly rather than fabricating success.
PRD section 9.1 properties (hierarchy, whitespace, typography scale, icon usage, task density, control alignment, absence of prohibited patterns) are judged on the auth shell and Today surfaces.
PRD section 9.2 behaviors (empty inbox next action, network error with preserved input and explicit retry) are demonstrated live on the implemented views.
Server-side authorization gates every private entity operation, and user data is isolated by user id at the data access boundary.
deferred_items: Calendar month and agenda views with user-timezone date rules.
Focus mode start, pause, resume, finish, and cancel states plus focus history.
Reminder scheduling, idempotent email delivery, delivery states, retries, and unsubscribe or preferences access.
Project board view with Planned, In progress, and Done columns, drag and drop, and its keyboard-accessible alternative.
Forgot-password and password-reset flows plus the account deletion request.
Inbox search and priority, due, and completion filters.
Settings depth beyond this slice: profile editing, timezone change, notification preferences, and session management.
implied_completion: Completing this slice implies the release path's remaining steps (focus session lifecycle, reminder email delivery with a safe link, logout re-verification) become the next loops' increments.
The app shell navigation implies Calendar, Focus, and Settings surfaces must reach implemented states in later loops; until then they render intentional styled empty states rather than dead links.
Once SQLite persistence exists, later entity additions (Reminder, Subtask, FocusSession, ActivityEvent) must evolve the schema without destroying existing user data.
mandatory_objectives: Deliver a runnable Tauri desktop application from the current bootstrap scaffold with a native window and the signed-in app shell.
Implement durable account registration, email verification through a local mail sink, sign in, session persistence, and sign out with server-side enforcement.
Implement title-only task quick-add and project creation backed by SQLite so data survives a full application restart.
Apply the PRD section 9 visual direction to the auth shell and implemented views with intentional empty, loading, and error states.
task_specification.objective: Turn the bootstrap scaffold into the first runnable Focusboard vertical slice: a native Tauri desktop app with durable account registration and email verification via a local mail sink, sign-in sessions that persist, SQLite-backed task quick-add and project creation, and the PRD section 9 visual direction on the auth shell, Inbox, Today, and Projects, so the prd_implementation_review gate has real candidate-bound runtime, interface, persistence, security, and visual evidence to evaluate.

diagnosis.root_cause: The gap prd_implementation_review is unverified because the candidate is a bare bootstrap scaffold: it contains only stub manifests (src-tauri/Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json) and a placeholder icon, with no Rust entry point, no frontend, no persistence, and no auth, so no runtime, interface, persistence, security, or visual evidence exists for the phase review to evaluate.

stop_conditions: Stop and report blocked if the Tauri scaffold cannot build or launch a native window in the development environment after a bounded toolchain effort; do not substitute a browser-only mock.
Stop and report blocked if the local mail sink cannot expose the verification message for scripted consumption; do not mark accounts verified without the real token flow.
Never present static mockups or edited screenshots as runtime visual evidence; if the visual bar cannot be met, stop with captured evidence of what fails.
Do not expand into deferred surfaces (calendar, focus, reminders, board drag and drop, settings depth) even when time remains; record the remaining work for the next loop instead.
If SQLite persistence cannot be made durable across restart, stop and report the failing layer rather than shipping in-memory state that silently loses data.

strategy.rationale: The phase review evaluates runtime, interface, persistence, security, and visual evidence, none of which the bare scaffold can produce; the smallest coherent increment that unblocks it is the first-run foundation: a runnable native shell, durable auth with mail-sink verification, SQLite-backed task capture, and the section 9 visual bar on implemented views, deferring calendar, focus, reminders, and board interaction to later loops.

code: The Rust crate compiles cleanly with cargo check and the frontend build completes without type or bundler errors before handoff.
No plaintext password comparison or logged token exists, and auth endpoints enforce the documented attempt-limiting protection.
runtime: The focusboard-native-webdriver replay drives the real desktop app through register, mail-sink verification, sign in, quick-add, project assignment, restart, and session persistence, and focusboard-verify exports runtime_state and source receipts.
visual: Captured screenshots of the auth shell, Inbox, Today, and Projects at wide and narrow window sizes show the PRD section 9 direction and match the section 9.1 board properties.
The empty inbox and network-error-with-preserved-input states from the section 9.2 board are captured live from the running app.

done_when: The candidate builds and launches a native desktop window through the Tauri runtime showing the Focusboard auth shell rather than a browser tab.
From cleared data, a user can register with a valid email and password, receive the verification email in the local mail sink, consume its single-use link, and sign in successfully.
An unverified, signed-out, or expired-session caller receives an explicit server-side authentication rejection on private operations, and the UI routes to sign in without data loss.
After signing in, the session and all created data survive a full application restart, backed by SQLite as the authoritative store for User, Session, EmailToken, Project, and Task records.
Quick-add creates a title-only task from the shell and keyboard shortcut without reload, rejects an empty title while preserving valid input, and the task can be assigned to a created project.
A task with today's due date appears in Today, a task without a due date remains only in Inbox and its project, and sign out returns to the auth shell.

Captured auth shell, Inbox, Today, and Projects views follow PRD section 9 direction with icon-plus-text navigation, visible focus states, restrained accent, and intentional empty, loading, and error states.
Auth failure feedback preserves the entered email, explains the next action, never reveals whether an unrelated email exists, and no password or token is written to logs or returned to the client.
tasks.instructions: Replace the bootstrap stub with the first runnable vertical slice of the Focusboard first-run path (PRD sections 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 6.2, 8, 9). Ship a native Tauri desktop application that builds and launches a real window showing the auth shell. Implement registration with email and password policy feedback, single-use expiring verification tokens delivered through a local development mail sink, sign in, session persistence across refresh, sign out, and explicit server-side rejection of private operations without a valid session, with passwords hashed, attempt limiting on auth endpoints, and no secrets in logs. Back the User, Session, EmailToken, Project, and Task entities with SQLite as the one authoritative server representation. Implement title-only quick-add with keyboard shortcut, empty-title rejection that preserves valid input, appearance without reload, project create and rename, task-to-project assignment, and Today, Inbox, and Projects views where a due-today task appears in Today and an undated task stays in Inbox and its project only. Apply PRD section 9 direction with intentional loading, empty, error, and retry states on every implemented surface; the exact module split is the Developer's choice within the listed edit surface.

risk_note.summary: This first slice spans build tooling, auth, persistence, three views, and the visual bar, so the likeliest insufficient_evidence outcome is a failure to launch or drive the app in the host webdriver environment.
risk_note.validation: Developer self-validates launch plus the register-verify-signin-quickadd-restart path with local receipts before handoff; host replay then recaptures runtime_state and screenshot evidence.
risk_note.why_now: Loop 1 has zero runtime evidence; establishing the runnable shell now is the prerequisite for every later surface and for the phase review to evaluate anything.
